headline: Approved Walmart site plan at 11 Ashleigh Drive and a mural at 20 Folsom Road; regional-impact finding for 24 Worthley Road failed.
summary: Ashleigh Drive Property Owner, LLC received a two-year extension, to December 3, 2028, for its approved plan. Brian Corliss questioned whether the 24 Worthley Road lot has frontage on a town-approved road, and that hearing was continued to November 4, 2026. Walmart's plan adds a 6,054 square foot online pickup and delivery area, and two escrow releases were approved.
decisions: Approved release #1 of $66,570.50 from Euro Stop cash escrow, 9-0.
Approved final release of $22,626.25 from 7 A Street cash escrow, 9-0.
Approved the September 16, 2026 minutes, 8-0 with one abstention.
Approved a two-year extension of the site plan approval for 41 Ashleigh Drive and 37 Scobie Pond Road, to December 3, 2028, 8-0 with one abstention.
Approved the Royal T Carwash mural at 20 Folsom Road as appropriate for the Industrial II district, 9-0.
Approved accepting jurisdiction over the two-lot subdivision at 24 Worthley Road, 9-0.
Denied a finding that the 24 Worthley Road subdivision is a development of regional impact, 9-0.
Approved a site walk at 24 Worthley Road on Saturday, October 17th at 1pm, 9-0.
Continued the 24 Worthley Road subdivision hearing to Wednesday, November 4th, 2026, 9-0.
Approved accepting jurisdiction over the amended Walmart site plan at 11 Ashleigh Drive, 9-0.
Denied a finding that the Walmart addition at 11 Ashleigh Drive is a development of regional impact, 9-0.
Approved a waiver to allow 9' x 18' parking stalls at 11 Ashleigh Drive, 9-0.
Found the Walmart application substantially complies with the Architectural Design Regulations, 9-0.
Approved the Findings of Fact for the Walmart application, 9-0.
Approved the Walmart site plan amendment at 11 Ashleigh Drive with conditions, 9-0.
Continued the zoning ordinance compliance workshop to a future meeting, with no objections.

transcript:
The Planning Board for the Town of Derry held a public meeting on Wednesday, October 07, 2026, at 7:00 p.m. The meeting was broadcast from the Derry Municipal Center, 14 Manning Street, Third Floor meeting room, with a virtual option.

Members present: Dave Nelson, Chair, John O'Connor, Vice Chair, Richard Malaby, Secretary, Randy Chase, Town Council Liaison, Brian Chirichiello, Town Administrator Representative, and Derek Minervini and Michael Wood, Members, and Thomas Mauzy, Z. Michael Appleton, and Andrew Young, Alternates

Members absent: Bryan Fishman and Jacob Pelletier, Members

Also present: Elizabeth Robidoux, Planning Director, Samuel Fazioli, Engineering Coordinator, and Caroline Wilson, Planning Administrative Secretary II

Mr. Nelson opened the meeting at 7:00 p.m. The meeting began with a salute to the flag.

Mr. Young was seated for Mr. Fishman and Mr. Mauzy was seated for Mr. Pelletier.

## Escrow

**#26-35**

**Project Name: Euro Stop, 5 B Street**

**Developer: 5 B Street, LLC**

**Escrow Account: Same**

**Escrow Type: Cash Escrow**

**Parcel ID/Location: 08001-010, 5 B Street**

The request is to approve Release #1 in the amount of $66,570.50 for the above noted project. The balance remaining of cash escrow will be $114,528.50. This escrow is non-interest bearing.

Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, to approve Escrow #26-35 as presented.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Wood, Minervini, O'Connor, Young, Chirichiello, Mauzy, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

**#26-36**

**Project Name: 7 A Street Change of Use**

**Developer: Durabull Trailers, LLC**

**Escrow Account: Same**

**Escrow Type: Cash Escrow**

**Parcel ID/Location: 08001-003, 7 A Street**

The request is to approve a final release of cash escrow in the amount of $22,626.25, for the above noted project. This escrow is non-interest bearing and the amount to retain is zero.

Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby to approve Escrow #26-36 as presented.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Wood, Minervini, O'Connor, Young, Chirichiello, Mauzy, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

## Minutes

The Board reviewed the minutes of the September 16, 2026 public meeting.

Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, to approve the minutes of the September 16, 2026 public meeting as written.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Wood, Minervini, O'Connor, Young, Mauzy, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. Chirichiello abstained due to being absent. The motion passed.

## Correspondence

Mr. Malaby announced that the Windham ZBA notified the Town of Derry of a hearing on October 15 at 6:30pm for the development of an indoor athletic complex at 39 Roulston Road, deemed a Development of Regional Impact. The Board had no comments to share with the Town of Windham.

## Other Business

### Fourth Extension Request

**PID 08017/08017-001, 41 Ashleigh Dr./37 Scobie Pond Rd.**

**Ashleigh Drive Property Owner, LLC**

Ms. Robidoux explained the two projects are located at the top of the Ashleigh Drive cul de sac. The original approvals were granted on January 3, 2024, when the lot was owned by Ashleigh Development, LLC. The property changed hands in September of 2025. Since that date, the new owner has been working to secure the necessary State approvals and finalize the Conservation Commission easement. The request letter attached to the staff report outlines the progress made to complete the conditions of approval. The new owner would like additional time to secure escrow for the two projects and to finalize the site plans.

For the record, the original approval was granted on January 3, 2024, with a 12 month period to meet conditions. The first extension (for 6 months) was granted in December, 2024. The second extension, also for 6 months was granted, in May of 2025. During this time, the property was changing hands. The third extension was granted for a period of one year in October, 2025 and will expire December 3, 2026. Given the amount of time it took to secure and finalize the conservation easement, it would not be impractical to grant the applicant more time to finalize the plan. This would be the 4th extension of the approval.

Staff recommends the Board permit the applicant additional time to finalize the plan and establish escrow, as requested.

Ms. Robidoux verified the project's timeline at Mr. Chirichiello's request.

Hayley Palazola, representative for Ashleigh Drive Property Owner, LLC, was recognized by the Board.

Ms. Palazola explained Ashleigh Drive Property Owner, LLC, purchased the property in September of 2025. Ms. Palazola appeared before the Board approximately one year ago, requesting additional time to finalize conditions, which included establishment of the Conservation easement. The process was lengthier than Ms. Palazola had expected; the involved parties went back and forth a couple of times on the stewardship plan, which was finalized in March of 2026, and was then approved by NHDES and NH Fish & Game. The easement signage language was created, the signage created, and the signs installed every 75' along the perimeter. Now that the easement plan and deed have been recorded, the applicant is working on the final conditions of the original approval. They have met with Town Engineering staff regarding some additional value engineering design modifications to the plan, such as lowering the site. The site will be marketed for additional users.

Mr. O'Connor mentioned that this and other developments are experiencing long wait times for their permits to be processed by NHDES and NH Fish & Game. Mr. Nelson added that he feels for the applicant.

Mr. Chirichiello inquired about the request for a two year long extension. Mr. Nelson added that given the complexity of the project, two years was not unreasonable. Ms. Palazola explained that she requested two years so that she would not have to request another extension in a year. It is a very large industrial project - finalizing designs, putting up escrow, financing the project, and finding tenants are still pending. Mr. Chirichiello felt that a two year extension was acceptable.

Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, to approve a two year extension (4th extension) of the conditional site plan approval granted to Ashleigh Drive Property Owner, LLC, PID 08017, 41 Ashleigh Drive and PID 08017-001, 37 Scobie Pond Road. The new expiration date will be December 03, 2028.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Wood, Minervini, Young, Chirichiello, Mauzy, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. O'Connor abstained, as he has for other votes for this project, as he is a direct abutter. The motion passed.

### Proposed Mural

**PID 35014-005, 20 Folsom Rd.**

**Brian & Laura Real Estate, LLC**

Ms. Robidoux explained the owners of Royal T car wash have proposed the addition of a mural to the eastern wall of the facility. The Board has been provided a rendering of the mural.

The Town of Derry Planning Board has the authority, per the Land Development Control Regulations, Section 170-83.A, to review changes that would affect the exterior of a building. Specifically in Section 170-84.A.3, alterations to structures within the Industrial II zoning district shall have a Medium High level of compliance with the regulations. Section 170-86.F.8 speaks to the color of a building, and specifically states 'subtle colors are appropriate on larger, plainer buildings, whereas smaller buildings with more detailing can more effectively incorporate brighter colors. Bright colors should be limited to accent areas. High intensity colors, metallic colors, or fluorescent colors should not be used'.

Staff recommends the Board review the proposal and make Findings of Fact.

Mr. Nelson added that the IND-II district was not as sensitive as some other districts in Town. This parcel is on the border of a commercial district and is within the Exit 4A Gateway District. Mr. Chirichiello appreciated the local historical elements incorporated into the mural, such as Alan Shepard Jr., the East Derry Church, and Hood Milk.

Mr. Chase agreed with Mr. Chirichiello. Mr. Chase suggested the milk carton might be Ross Dairy to represent the dairy that used to stand at the location.

Mr. Mauzy inquired if the mural would be externally illuminated. Ms. Robidoux was unsure; and none of the applicants' representatives were present to ask. Typically businesses are asked to turn their lights off when they are not open. Mr. Mauzy was concerned with the light interfering with traffic coming off of the highway. Mr. Nelson stated the mural will be on the wall facing Tsienneto Road. Still, having bright lights in the evening when visibility is lower might be distracting to motorists.

Mr. Appleton inquired about the mural's installation. Ms. Robidoux explained that typically the design is projected onto the surface, it is traced, and then filled in by the artist. Mr. Nelson added that the Board's action tonight is to approve this in concept; the Board does not have complete artistic control but should ensure the mural sets an appropriate tone for the district.

Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, after review of the proposal, the Board finds the proposed mural to be located on the east wall of Royal T Carwash, PID 35014-005, 20 Folsom Road is appropriate for the Industrial II Zoning District as:

The proposed change demonstrates overall compliance with the Architectural Design Regulations.

The proposed change does not detrimentally affect the nature of the surrounding uses, the style of the surrounding buildings, or special feature of historic, cultural or community interest in the vicinity of the project.

The proposed colors are appropriate for the neighborhood and the district.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Wood, Minervini, O'Connor, Young, Chirichiello, Mauzy, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

## Planning Director / Chairman Updates

Ms. Robidoux mentioned that the Planning Department will be closed on October 21st through 23rd, as staff will be in attendance at the NNECAPA Conference. There will not be a Planning Board meeting on October 21st; the next scheduled meeting will be November 4th.

Ms. Robidoux wished to confirm that the Board was content holding two meetings in December (the 2nd and 16th) - there were no objections.

James Vayo with SNHPC will present The Existing Conditions Analysis of the three target areas for the Housing Readiness Action Plan to the Board at the November 4th meeting.

The two cases before the Board this evening were processed through the GovWell portal; the Board will notice the new appearance of the application summary pages.

The new version of DerryNH.gov has just gone live; there are some broken links that staff plan to correct by the end of next week.

Mr. Nelson announced that four Board members (along with planners from around the State) met here at the Municipal Center on 9/24 for a Plans Reading and Analysis workshop, presented by Sylvia von Aulock. The workshop provided a method to color code plans for analysis, as well as standard engineering symbology. Mr. Nelson hopes that color coding of plans will be facilitated for members for future plan reviews.

## Nottonson Family Revocable Trust

**Nottonson Stephen J./Karen E., Trustees**

**PID 12006, 24 Worthley Road**

**Acceptance/Review**

**Two Lot Subdivision**

Ms. Robidoux explained the property is located in the LDR zoning district which requires a minimum of three acres and 200 feet of frontage per lot. The ZBA granted a variance on December 18, 2025, to permit the lots to be subdivided with less than the required frontage. The parent parcel consists of 9.9 acres of land. The subdivision will reduce the parent lot (24 Worthley) to 6.856 acres with 100.07 feet of frontage. The new lot will be 3 acres with 72.09 feet of frontage.

There is an existing access easement that benefits Parcel 12010, currently owned by the Corliss family; this runs along the southeast portion of the property where the parent and proposed lot have access. Ms. Robidoux's original understanding was that this easement was not used by the Corliss family, as their main access is on Chester Road. After discussion with the Corliss family, Ms. Robidoux learned the Corlisses do utilize the Worthley Road easement in the winter; as the slopes and length to get out to Chester Road is not navigable in the winter. There is a right of way easement granted by the Town of Derry (Plan D-37044, December 2010), which was part of the right of way acceptance by the Town at that time. It is this right of way easement from which the lot has frontage on a town approved road.

The surveyor addressed all of the TRC comments. The new parcel is being assigned an address of 22.5 Worthley Road and a PID of 12006-001.

Waiver requests include:

1. LDCR Section 170-25.A (25) driveway access through its own frontage
2. LDCR Section 170-25.B, lot sizing by soils
3. LDCR Section 170-25.A (2) lots lines at right angles
4. LDCR Section 170-25.G, monumentation
5. LDCR Section 170-26.A (16.a.iv), sight distance profile for driveways

A State Subdivision approval will be required.

Staff recommends the Board review the project for regional impact and review the submitted plan.

Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, to accept jurisdiction of the 2 lot subdivision plan before the Board for Karen & Stephen Nottonson, PID 12006, 24 Worthley Road.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Wood, Minervini, O'Connor, Young, Chirichiello, Mauzy, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

Motion by Malaby, seconded by Malaby, pursuant to RSA 36:56, the Board finds the proposal as presented at this time meets the definition of a development of regional impact.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Wood, Minervini, O'Connor, Young, Chirichiello, Mauzy, Malaby, and Nelson vote No, this is a small subdivision near the center of Town, not near any municipal boundaries, therefore it does not meet the definition of a development of regional impact.

Motion by Chirichiello, seconded by Malaby, to open the Public Hearing.

All members present vote Yes. The motion passed.

Neal McCarthy with Promised Land Survey was recognized by the Board.

Mr. McCarthy explained that the variance granted allowed the lots to contain less than the required frontage, and both lots will contain greater than the required land area. There are no wetlands on the site. Aside from the parcel's access, Mr. McCarthy did not feel this proposal was remarkable.

Mr. Nelson inquired about the longstanding easement, which appears to be along the front edge of the new parcel. Where it connects to something else is off of the map.

Mr. McCarthy explained that the easement sweeps off to the westerly side of the plan, and that is how it gets up to the Corliss property. It is depicted on the plan set for about 50' beyond the subject parcels. Mr. McCarthy stated that the easement was used seasonally.

Mr. Nelson invited members of the Public to comment.

**Brian Corliss**, 111 Chester Road (PID 12010), was recognized by the Board.

Mr. Corliss provided history for the Board. In 1978, Mr. Corliss purchased the parcel, which at that time included the parcels now known as 12010 and 12006. In 1985, Mr. Corliss applied to subdivide the lot, creating PIDs 12010 and 12006 as they are presently configured. In order to obtain approval from the Planning Board and ZBA, Mr. Corliss had Worthley Road paved.

In 2011, the residents of Worthley Road petitioned the Town to accept Worthley Road. The road's status was subsequently upgraded from private to town approved. When the ZBA reviewed the plan, the question remained, "where is Worthley Road?" Mr. Corliss explained that Worthley Road starts at Beaver Lake on North Shore Road. Mr. Corliss believed that Worthley Road ends on the southern end between 12006 and the Dionne property (12007 / 22 Worthley Road).

In order to build his family's home, Mr. Corliss widened the area (visible in the lower left corner of the plan) in 1978, creating a "turnabout." It does not meet cul de sac standards, but Mr. Corliss did the best he could to widen it to create a path through the woods, up the hill, to where he built his home. Mr. Corliss brought in sand and gravel and brought the grade up a couple of feet, and scraped the crest of the hill down to bedrock to make it as accessible as possible. Mr. Corliss stated the Town assumed Worthley Road in 2011, but only to where it stops on the lot line to the Dionne property down to the turnabout. Mr. Corliss stated the Town then created a right of way overlapping the turnabout Mr. Corliss created.

Mr. Corliss felt there were three problems with granting approval for this subdivision. Firstly, it is difficult to get up the hill. Secondly, when up there, it is difficult and hazardous to come back down, especially when approaching the blind intersection. After 46 years of trying, Mr. Corliss stated it is not possible to get up that way in the winter.

The third problem: Mr. Corliss reviewed the ZBA minutes of 12/18/2025; it was stated that PID 12006 has 100' of frontage on an approved road - Worthley Road. It also states that 12006-001 would have 72' of frontage. Mr. Corliss disagreed, and felt that the 72' was on a right of way, not an approved road. Mr. Corliss believes 12006-001 remains totally within 12006 and therefore has no true frontage.

Mr. Nelson asked who were the beneficiaries of the viatic easement. Mr. Corliss stated that he and his family are. Mr. Nelson did not think that was a public right of way, but a private right of way for the Corliss' benefit.

Mr. Corliss stated there was a right of way and an easement. The Public Utilities Commission (PUC) has an easement including four utility poles. The PUC has a right to come up anytime, and they do come up and clear brush. Mr. Corliss stated that he and his family are the sole beneficiaries of the right of way. Who is responsible for maintaining an easement? The utility clears the lines, but the neighbor is responsible for maintaining and paving the patch, which Mr. Corliss stated he has done for many years. When subdividing in 1985, Mr. Corliss specifically ensured that he himself is listed as the owner of the right of way is in the deed and in the title.

The driveway as proposed was supposed to come down upon Mr. Corliss' right of way, and may cause future obstructions. Mr. Corliss plans to continue to maintain his right of way. Mr. Corliss encouraged the Board to consider that the proposed parcel does not contain frontage on a Town approved road.

Mr. Nelson invited Mr. McCarthy to respond to Mr. Corliss' concerns thus far. Mr. McCarthy stated that he would have to research the exact location of the terminus of the publicly maintained portion of Worthley Road. Mr. McCarthy explained that, in prior years, Promised Land Survey surveyed the entire length of Worthley Road for the purpose of Town acceptance of the road. Mr. McCarthy felt the area at the end was potentially part of what was approved, although it could just be in the easement. Reexamination will need to occur to determine the actual terminus of the road.

Mr. Nelson asked Mr. Fazioli if DPW maintains files on every publicly accepted Town road; Mr. Fazioli said yes, along with the Town Clerks' office. Mr. O'Connor explained that many years ago, there was an issue with effluent flowing into Beaver Lake. With that, the Town installed a wastewater system. Inadvertently, the road acceptance only went partly up Worthley Road, and had to be re-accepted. Mr. O'Connor is unsure but believes the Planning Board and the Town Council had to accept every location off of the sewer pipe. Mr. O'Connor is unsure where Worthley Road stops.

Ms. Robidoux recalled when it was petitioned to start accepting some of the roads around Beaver Lake, Worthley Road was presented in three sections; A, B, and C. Section B is what Mr. O'Connor spoke of, with sewer. Section C came up to the end where it says "See plan reference number 3" on the plan. To the best of her knowledge and recollection, Ms. Robidoux believed the accepted portion of Worthley Road ends right after the turnaround that Mr. Corliss created at the driveway leading to the current Nottonson driveway and residence.

Mr. Nelson stated there did not appear to be a northerly boundary of the easement within the bounds of the subject property - how far did "section C" extend toward the top of the page? Ms. Robidoux's understanding was that on sheet 3, one can see where Worthley comes in, and there is a kind of terminus, with a line that leads to the Nottonsons, and another line that leads to the south (the Scott property) – that is where Wortley ended. Mr. Nelson suggested the Board obtain the easement documents.

Mr. Corliss referred to a Derry Public Works staff report dated September 20, 2011. It explains that the Town has sought right of way on the Nottonson property, overlapping the turnabout Mr. Corliss made. The right of way still exists, and the proposed lot is only on the right of way. Mr. Corliss suggested that if the subdivision does proceed, that the driveway be brought straight down and enjoin the Nottonson driveway. Mr. Corliss felt the challenge the Board will face is whether to approve two lots together on limited frontage. Mr. Corliss felt there were errors made during the ZBA meeting of 12/18/2025; it was stated by Mr. Peloquin (not present) and Mr. McCarthy that Worthley Road was depicted as an old historic road and they were not sure where the end of it was. Mr. Corliss was sure where the end of Worthley Road was, and he showed the Board a plat that he has had in his possession. Mr. Corliss clarified that he does use the section in question as his auxiliary driveway.

Mr. Nelson would prefer to clarify the matter for the Corliss family. Mr. Nelson was not sure if the ZBA acted on factual information or if they made assumptions based on cloudy history. Mr. Nelson suggested the proposed driveway as shown on sheet 3 traverses the easement. Mr. Nelson was curious how that works.

Ms. Robidoux accessed the recorded plan from the Registry of Deeds; the easements appeared to be multilayered. Where the 50' ROW is, Worthley Road comes in, and almost where the frontage for the new lot's access begins, a sort of trapezoid area encompasses the turnaround area and the line where the 50' easement ends. That is the accepted portion of Worthley Road – also known as "area D."

Mr. Nelson examined "area D," a ROW easement comprising 4,362 SF, in a trapezoidal shape. Ms. Robidoux explained that the right of way itself goes over parcel 12006's lot line, goes across 50', and ends. There is a right of way easement and a viatic easement on the same location. Different parties are benefitted by each layer. When the Town accepted Worthley Road, was area D accepted as public? Ms. Robidoux said yes, that is how the Nottonsons have access on a public road and would be able to subdivide. In order to have substandard frontage, the Nottonsons got a variance from the ZBA. It was deemed that it was appropriate to allow the ~70+' of frontage for the new lot.

Mr. Corliss respectfully suggested that on 9/20/2011, the Town obtained a ROW so that the public could use it; but the Town did not seize that portion. Mr. Nelson explained that the Town can grant a viatic easement in favor of the Town, and then can accept that portion of the road as Public. Mr. Corliss referred to the two iron pins to be placed by PLS; would this be creating acceptable frontage? Mr. Nelson stated that if the Town Council accepted Worthley Road – including the area referred to as the turnabout – as a public road, then a boundary that goes up to the boundary of the ROW easement boundary is considered frontage on a public road. It all depends on what the Town Council voted to do.

Mr. Corliss reminded the Board of the difficulty of this access [in winter]. Mr. Corliss strongly encouraged the Board to come and examine the site in-person prior to making a decision.

Mr. Nelson asked Mr. McCarthy about the existing and proposed topo lines on the plan. Mr. McCarthy confirmed the solid lines are proposed grading that would need to occur as that section is very steep. It was confirmed that the proposed grading would be on the proposed lot. Mr. Nelson inquired of the percentage grade of the post development condition. Mr. McCarthy explained the design was suited to the Town's requirements, and was 14.8% where 15% is the maximum allowed.

Mr. Fazioli explained the Town has strict requirements for the first 40' of driveways. The proposed grade is going to be flatter than what exists. There should be earthwork to taper off the sides of the driveway.

Mr. Corliss did not believe it was possible to flatten the turnabout area any more. Mr. Corliss brought the grade up with machinery as much as he could in the years past. Mr. Corliss is concerned about drainage. Mr. Corliss stated Mr. Nottonson has tried to control drainage, and Mr. Corliss suggested the Town will have to put in some kind of drainage to capture the water that will come off of the hill.

Mr. O'Connor suggested the Board obtain the original documents for the acceptance of Worthley Road before making any decisions on this proposal; Mr. Chase agreed, and that at the very least the case should be continued. Mr. Chase would have a hard time approving this plan tonight.

Mr. Nelson stated that as long as the post development runoff does not exceed the predevelopment runoff, then the Board is required to approve the proposed drainage. Mr. Nelson asked the Board if they wished to do a site walk. Mr. O'Connor stated that parking will be difficult; Mr. Nelson suggested carpooling.

Mr. Nelson confirmed with the property owner, Karen Nottonson, that it will be acceptable to hold a site walk open to the public at that time.

Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, to schedule a site walk at 24 Worthley Road on Saturday, October 17th at 1pm.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Wood, Minervini, O'Connor, Young, Chirichiello, Mauzy, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

Motion by O'Connor, seconded by Malaby, to continue the hearing for the 2 lot subdivision plan for Karen & Stephen Nottonson, PID 12006, 24 Worthley Road to Wednesday, November 4th, 2026.

Roll Call Vote: Chase, Wood, Minervini, O'Connor, Young, Chirichiello, Mauzy, Malaby, and Nelson vote Yes. The motion passed.

Mr. Nelson reminded attendees that no additional written notice of the continuation of the meeting will be posted or mailed to abutters.

**Wal-Mart Real Estate Business Trust**

**PID 08279, 11 Ashleigh Drive**

**Acceptance/Review**

**Site Plan Amendment – Addition of 6,054 SF Online Pickup and Delivery Area**

Ms. Robidoux explained the proposal is to add a 6,054 square foot addition to the existing Walmart facility located on Ashleigh Drive. The purpose of the addition is to enhance Walmart's online pickup and delivery options. The existing online pickup area located closest to the Pharmacy will be discontinued. The new addition will be constructed adjacent to the current outdoor/garden area.

To accommodate the new building addition and use, a total of .66 acres will be disturbed, which falls below the requirement to update the Storm Water Pollution Protection Plan (SWPPP). The water main located in this area will be relocated. A new parking area is being designated for online pickup. The five trees/island currently located to the east of the main building will be removed to accommodate the proposal. Six trees will be planted in a grassed area behind the building so that the site can continue to comply with the landscape requirements. Four new light poles will be installed and three existing light heads will be replaced in order to provide increased lighting intended to provide a safe environment for employees and customers.

Site changes include the elimination of a landscaped island and removal of greenspace to the northeast of the existing building. This area is being set aside for temporary outdoor storage containers. A snow storage area was added just in front of the area proposed for the storage containers. As part of the proposal, areas to the rear of the lot will be set aside to accommodate the permanent and seasonal storage containers.

Temporary storage containers are on site between October and December, and three permanent storage containers will remain to the rear of the existing building. (see Sheet SSM-1). Ten temporary storage containers will be located on the new asphalt area to the northeast side of the site and four temporary trailers will be located on 10 parking spaces located to the east of the new building addition.

Access to the site does not change. Wayfinding will be installed to direct people along the rear of the parking lot to the new online pickup area to avoid conflicts with pedestrian traffic along the front of the existing store. There will be a dedicated pickup area that is clearly signed and striped, along with a dedicated employee path with controlled dispensing areas. This proposal does not affect the existing emergency access road.

The parking requirements are still met, even with the construction of additional parking spaces. For this use, one parking space per 300 square feet of retail use is required. With the addition, 558 spaces are required for the total site. The applicant is providing 687 spaces.

A traffic summary and drainage report were provided with the application. Both show that there are no anticipated negative impacts. Representatives from Colliers Engineering confirmed that the truck turning movements will continue to be accommodated around the building without conflicts, even with the addition of the three permanent and three temporary storage containers.

Utilities will be relocated to accommodate the project. DPW can best address any questions with regard to those changes.

Requested waivers include LDCR Section 170-63.C (1), parking stall width and length.

Local permits will be required.

Staff recommends the Board determine regional impact, review proposed changes, confirm number and location of temporary and permanent storage containers and seasonal items.
